full_sentence: Walking along the river, I saw an old friend.

options.why_wrong: The participle clause refers to the subject of the main clause, and a river cannot walk, so this is illogical.
This describes a state, but the main clause must say what the walking person did or saw.

options.text: I will walk for a long time.
options.why_wrong: The main clause should describe what happened during the walk, and this only adds a future plan.

grammar_focus: Participle clauses with a shared subject
explanation: The -ing clause at the start must describe the same person as the main clause subject. Learners should check that the person doing the walking is also the one who sees the friend.
translation: Nehir boyunca yürürken eski bir arkadaşımı gördüm.
